key_insight: Short-fiber reinforcement increases mean local apparent indentation modulus in PBT while reducing mean indentation creep depth and increasing spatial heterogeneity.
engineering_relevance: A controlled indentation protocol enables spatially resolved stiffness and creep assessment in heterogeneous injection-molded PBT components.
method: Use unreinforced PBT to assess indentation spacing, surface preparation, load, timing, and unloading evaluation.
Compare indentation loads of 500, 1000, and 1750 mN; polish surfaces to reduce topographical disturbances.
Apply a final 1750 mN protocol with 6 s loading, 300 s holding, and 4 s unloading to unreinforced and short-fiber-reinforced PBT.
evidence_signal: Mean apparent indentation modulus increases from 2.91 to 6.65 GPa, mean creep depth decreases from 2.36 to 1.91 µm, and coefficients of variation increase for both quantities with reinforcement.
watch_item: Quantitative results depend on surface preparation and load history; apparent indentation modulus should not be treated as protocol-independent bulk stiffness.
paper_title: Methodological Assessment of Instrumented Indentation for Spatially Resolved Mesoscale Stiffness and Creep in Short Fiber-Reinforced Injection-Molded PBT Components
